transcript:
[15:00] Meeting header: 2025-11-12 15:00 PST | Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Gupta (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Martin Kline (Orion Head of Infrastructure), Priya Desai (CTO), Jules Park (Security Architect), Rina Cho (DevOps), Alexei Moroz (Platform)

Summary: quick discovery focused on Private / VPC deployment. Customer wants to host inference inside their VPC with private connectivity to Redwood control plane; they asked about peering, private endpoints, region restrictions, and KMS/BYOK.

[15:02] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Samir with Redwood, and with me is Lena our solutions engineer. big picture — we'd love to understand Orion's constraints for a private deployment, region needs, and security must-haves.

[15:03] Priya: thanks, Samir. quick context: we're a retail platform with PII tied to orders, and regulatory folks want no egress to public internet for inference. high level preference is a private deployment inside our VPC or a peered private endpoint. timeline is Q1 pilot.

[15:04] Lena: makes sense. to clarify, Redwood Private can be deployed two ways: 1) a customer VPC with VPC peering / Transit Gateway to Redwood's serving VPC, or 2) a fully private control plane where you run the inference nodes in your account/region (on-prem or bring-your-own-cloud). we'll dig into the network tradeoffs.

[15:05] Martin: on our side, we'd prefer Redwood-hosted control plane but with private peering — we want Redwood to manage the runtime but without public endpoints. can you do cross-account VPC peering? what about Transit Gateway?

[15:06] Lena: yes we support cross-account VPC peering and TGW. general patterns: peering is simple for single-VPC setups; TGW works better if you have many VPCs and need central routing. one caveat: peering is region-limited unless you use inter-region peering or TGW.

[15:07] Jules: for security, we need to know if you require AWS Direct Connect or if peering is enough. also, how do you handle DNS resolution — we need private DNS so model endpoints resolve to ENIs inside our VPC.

[15:07] Lena: good question. we offer private endpoints (VPC endpoints) and ENI-based network attachments. typical pattern: Redwood creates ENIs in your VPC that talk to the serving nodes; you control the CIDR ranges. DNS can be via Route53 private hosted zones or host-records we provide. we'll share the exact flow doc.

[15:08] Rina: any constraints on port ranges, MTU, or ephemeral port usage? our security team is strict about allowed ports.

[15:09] Lena: usually we use TLS over standard ports (443) for control plane, and intra-VPC traffic for tokenized requests may use custom ports for gRPC or raw TCP depending on the runtime. MTU is typically 1500; large payloads can trigger fragmentation so we recommend jumbo frames off. we'll include a port and MTU table in the network requirements doc.

[15:10] Priya: region-wise we need EU data residency for production — Amsterdam or Frankfurt. can Redwood host Private in eu-west-1 or eu-central-1?

[15:11] Samir: yes, we have Private deployments in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 for customers requiring residency. for hosted Dedicated we also have capacity in those regions. if you pick Redwood-hosted Private with peering, we'll ensure serving nodes are pinned to those regions.

[15:12] Martin: what about KMS? we need BYOK and the keys must never leave our account. how do you integrate for model encryption at rest and for traffic between control and serving plane?

[15:13] Lena: we support customer-managed KMS keys (BYOK). typical pattern is that the customer owns the CMK in their account and grants Redwood the necessary key usage perms via a cross-account role. keys remain in your account; we never export key material. for HSM-level requirements we can discuss an HSM-backed flow.

[15:14] Jules: policy-wise we need to record all calls and have audit logs centralized to our Splunk instance. can you push audit logs and request traces out to our logging pipeline?

[15:15] Samir: yes — we can stream audit logs (request/response meta) to your S3 or to a logging endpoint. common approach: logs to an S3 bucket in your account, and you configure lifecycle and access. we also offer webhook hooks for events. we'll add docs.

[15:16] Alexei: latency / throughput question — our peak is 120 QPS across user-facing features with p95 latency requirement ~200ms. if we go Private, what's the SLA and how does batching / KV cache behave inside peered setups?

[15:17] Lena: performance is largely identical — the runtime keeps KV caches local to the serving nodes. latency depends on cross-VPC path. with ENIs inside your VPC, network hop is minimal. we recommend a small performance runbook: pin model variants to nodes, enable prefix caching, and use our batching plugin. we'll provide recommended instance types and expected tokens/sec numbers per GPU.

[15:18] Rina: regarding NAT and egress: do you require outbound internet from our VPC for control-plane calls or image pulls? our infra blocks public egress except via a NAT gateway.

[15:19] Lena: image pulls can be done from internal registries or via a secure pipeline; for managed image fetches we can pull from a private S3 repo or provide signed images. control plane communication can be routed through private endpoints; we don't require public internet if you prefer. there may be exceptions for software updates unless you host update artifacts in your account.

[15:20] Jules: curious about failover: if we have multi-region requirement, does Redwood support active-active or active-passive cross-region replicas for the serving layer?

[15:21] Samir: we support multi-region deployments. commonly customers use an active-primary in their chosen region and a cold-standby or read-only deploy in a backup region. active-active is possible but requires careful KV cache syncing; we can help design that for low RPO/RTO needs.

[15:22] Priya: compliance question — do you have SOC2 reports and pen test results we can share with our InfoSec?

[15:23] Samir: yes, we'll share SOC 2 Type II, ISO artifacts, and a redacted pen test summary. for Private deployments we also provide an architecture security playbook showing the network flows and least-privilege IAM roles.

[15:25] Martin: on connectivity cost — we're worried about inter-region data transfer charges if requests route cross-region. if we pin to eu-west-1, can you guarantee traffic stays in-region?

[15:26] Lena: we can pin serving nodes to eu-west-1 and ensure peering is local. however control-plane callbacks might be in another region unless you opt for fully private control plane in your account. we'll include cost tradeoffs in the SOW.

[15:27] Rina: developer ergonomics — how will our app call the model endpoints? do you give SDKs for private endpoints?

[15:28] Lena: yes we surface the same HTTP/gRPC APIs as hosted Redwood, just pointing to private FQDNs. SDKs work unchanged; auth is via customer-issued tokens or mutual TLS depending on the config. we support SAML/SSO for console access and RBAC for team isolation.

[15:29] Alexei: curious about model updates — if we need a patch or model rollback, how do we orchestrate without exposing data? can rollouts be canaryed inside our VPC?

[15:30] Lena: rollouts are controllable — we support canary percentages and automatic fallback. for Private deployments you can choose rollout policies and retain logs in your S3. no model artifacts leave your environment if you opt for customer-hosted storage.

[15:31] Jules: any special firewall rules for webhook callbacks or health checks? we block all inbound except specific CIDR ranges.

[15:32] Samir: we typically provide a set of Redwood egress CIDRs or request you create security groups allowing the ENIs we attach. in some setups we ask for a cross-account role and we don't need inbound open ports beyond VPC ENI attachments. we'll provide the minimal CIDRs and health-check endpoints.

[15:34] Priya: what's your PKI model for mTLS? do you rotate certs automatically?

[15:35] Lena: we can support mTLS with certificates issued by Redwood or integrate with your internal PKI. cert rotation is automated; for BYOK or BYOC PKI we can accept cert bundles and rotate per your policy.

[15:36] Martin: on testing — we'd like to run a small POC with 10 QPS, validate latency, and test audit log delivery. what's a typical test plan?

[15:37] Lena: typical POC steps: 1) exchange CIDRs and IAM roles, 2) build peering/TGW, 3) attach ENIs and test DNS resolution, 4) run synthetic traffic at target QPS and collect p95/p99, 5) validate logs to S3 and Splunk. we'll send a one-page test-plan and a workbook for results.

[15:38] Jules: security requirement — we need an assurance that keys never leave account and logs are tamper-evident. can you support S3 Object Lock or signed log ingestion?

[15:39] Samir: yes we can write to an S3 bucket you own and you can enable Object Lock; we also support signed event hooks and can put logs into an append-only store. we'll include these options in the playbook.

[15:40] Rina: small nit — do you have constraints on ephemeral port ranges for large parallel connections? we'll be opening up many ephemeral ports for users.

[15:41] Lena: we'll include recommended ephemeral port ranges; in practice the runtime multiplexes connections and batching reduces parallel connections, but we'll call that out.

[15:42] Samir: ok great — recap: action items, Samir will send SOW + pricing and SOC2 and network docs; Lena will schedule the network deep-dive and send the POC test plan; Jules will provide CIDR and region preference (eu-west-1) by Friday; Orion to confirm pilot timeline Q1. any other blockers?

[15:43] Priya: none from me, thanks — looking forward to docs.

[15:44] Samir: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with artifacts and calendar invites.

[15:45] Meeting end.

Notes: transcript contains a few minor transcription artifacts — product names occasionally transcribed as 'Reedwood' or 'Redwood Dedicate', and speaker turns sometimes condensed. Shared artifacts referenced: 'network-requirements.pdf' (to be sent), 'SOC2-redacted.pdf', 'private-deploy-playbook.md', and 'poc-test-workbook.xlsx'.
